title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space and defense sectors are buzzing with contract awards and strategic partnerships, while the specter of budget adjustments looms large. As companies jockey for position in a rapidly evolving landscape, the stakes for innovation and resilience have never been higher.

themes.title: Mars Communications Orbiter RFP
themes.body: NASA has released its final request for proposals for a Mars communications orbiter, signaling a push for robust interplanetary communication. This could set the stage for future missions and collaborations in deep space exploration.

themes.title: Space Force Contracts Galore
themes.body: Northrop Grumman's $398 million satellite contract from the Space Force highlights the ongoing investment in military space capabilities. Meanwhile, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant has cleared a critical design review, indicating a competitive landscape for defense contracts.

themes.title: Funding and Budget Adjustments
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the importance of secure space operations. This influx of cash may fuel innovation but also raises questions about prioritization amid competing defense needs.

themes.title: Private Sector Moves
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round underscores the increasing interest in commercial space ventures. As companies like Cowboy Space propose massive satellite constellations, the race for data services in orbit is heating up.
